changes: Added 'vājapeyin' to the scribe's titles (ācāryavājappyayi = ācārya vājapeyī) instead of leaving it only in the notes
Normalized the residence: near Guhyeśvarī at Paśupati, belonging to Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa (Kathmandu)
Place of copying cleared: kāṣṭhapaṃḍapasthāna describes where the scribe belongs. It is not stated as the place of copying. Explained in notes
Notes expanded on the corrupt forms and the era

notes: The era is not named. 'saṃvat 1854' in a Devanagari MS fits VS; NS 1854 is impossible. VS 1854 Phālguna kṛṣṇa 8 falls around February–March 1798 CE. The name is written 'bhairavānda', a corrupt form of Bhairavānanda (the catalogue has Bairavānanda). 'vājappyayi(‥)' is read as vājapeyī, a brahmin title. The scribe is described as living near Guhyeśvarī at Paśupati, and the compound continues with 'kāṣṭhapaṃḍapasthāna' (Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa = Kathmandu). That part most likely describes where he belongs. It does not explicitly name the place of copying, though copying in the Kathmandu area is probable.
